body: `vp3_compatible` is always 0. I'm not sure if there's a reason to enable VP3 strict compatibility nowadays. We can probably remove it and the associated member in the header file.
`audio_bitrate` is always `0`, so the constant bitrate code (the `else` branch) is never run. We should remove it if there's no reason to use CBR over VBR.

body: I think that's a good default, although a lower value might improve the quality in some cases, and the granularity on seeks. It could be a good candidate for a setting.

The library default is false. The documentation doesn't even mention it, but I think it allows the encoder to be a bit loose about the bitrate target.

This is from the source:
```
/**Ignore bitrate buffer underflows.
 * If the encoder uses so many bits that the reservoir of available bits
 *  underflows, ignore the deficit.
 * The encoder will not try to make up these extra bits in future frames.
 * At low rates this may cause the result to be oversized; it should normally
 *  be disabled, which is the default.*/
```

I would remove the related code.
Same as with `soft-target`, I would leave it to the library defaults and remove all code.
